root_causes.cause: File25 index lease stale reclaim, owner release and final state publish still used non-atomic WordPress read/delete and read/update patterns; SQL race could overwrite or delete newer generation after PHP check.
root_causes.fix: Conditional BINARY serialized-value SQL DELETE for expected lease; conditional joined SQL UPDATE matches both lease and old running index before commit. WordPress cache invalidation after SQL. Production missing DB CAS backend fails closed.
root_causes.remaining: Actual MySQL/InnoDB/distributed object-cache and multi-worker stress acceptance not yet performed; isolated fake-WPDB query-level interleaving is narrower.

root_causes.cause: UpgradeManager conditional owner check followed by delete_option, so expired/finished worker could remove successor lock between PHP read and deletion.
root_causes.fix: Stale upgrade-lease reclamation and owned release now use conditional database SQL DELETE matching exact serialized lock; missing production backend refuses non-atomic fallback.
root_causes.remaining: Full production-like lock timing, migration and rollback not verified.

root_causes.cause: File25's File24 integration sliced the other modules to 98 and unconditionally unshifted its own manifest; when collection reached capacity this silently displaced other source-owner manifests.
root_causes.fix: Checked File24 v0.99.0 registry MAX_MANIFESTS=100 (self+99). Preserve unrelated module inputs; defer File25 under full registry, emit capacity blocked event and avoid truncation. Modify existing manifest behavioral test to cover limit boundary.
root_causes.remaining: Large over-capacity File24 registry itself reads its own bounded 99-item slice; File25 no longer introduces silent owner displacement.
